sentences.text:
National Insurance Company vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:10290
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On The 9 th Of May, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1225 of 2007
 National Insurance Company
 Versus
 Dilip Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Mr. Shriniwas Gajendragadkar - Advocate for the appel
 Insurance Company.
 Mr. Ramesh Prasad Gupta - Advocate for the respondent
 Order
The appellant - Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles
Act, challenging the award dated 06.10.2007 passed by 4th Additional Motor Accident, Claims
Tribunal, Mo

rena, in Claim Case No.111/2007, wherein the Insurance Company has been held liable to pay the amount of compensation to the claimants and has been given the rights to recover the amount from the owner/driver of the vehicle.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in view of the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal, the directions issued by the Tribunal to pay and recover the amount is unsustainable.
As per his submissions, since there is apparent breach of terms of policy, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to pay.
Therefore, he submits that the direction of Tribunal to pay and recover is unsustainable in law.

In view of the judgment rendered by this Court in the case of Ratna Parashar and others Vs.
Kusumlata and others, decided on 07.02.2008 in M.P.No.432/2008, the submission of the counsel for the appellant is not acceptable.

entities.text:
Ratna Parashar and others Vs.
Kusumlata and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court in para - 13 held as under :
"13. Having regard to the aforesaid facts we are of the considered opinion that New India Assurance Co. Ltd. cannot be held liable to indemnify the insured and they are accordingly absolved therefrom.

However, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in Swaran Singh's case MANU/SC/0021/2004 (SC) and Pramod Kumar National Insurance Company vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74740666/
1 Agarwal Vs. Mushtari Begum MANU/SC/0637/2004 (SC), let the insurer to pay the compensation fixed hereunder and recover 50 per cent of the same from the insured and remaining 50 per cent from the owner of truck which collided with the jeep."
4.

entities.text: Pramod Kumar National Insurance Company vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in view of the discussion made above, it cannot be held that the direction of the Tribunal to pay and then recover, passed against the Insurance Company is illegal.
5. In view of the aforesaid, no illegality is found in the award passed by the Claims Tribunal.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE bj/-
National Insurance Company vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74740666/
